title: UP Warriorz Sign Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 Crore at WPL Auction
excerpt: Australia's captain was the costliest buy in Kochi as UP Warriorz filled all eight open slots, brought back Grace Harris, and beat RCB in the day's biggest bidding contest.
body:
• Australia captain Sophie Molineux was the most expensive buy at the WPL 2027 auction in Kochi, joining UP Warriorz for INR 1.10 crore after Royal Challengers Bengaluru dropped out at INR 1.05 crore.
  • UP Warriorz filled all eight of their open slots, also bringing back Grace Harris for INR 30 lakh and signing Sneh Rana, Sushma Verma and Asha Sobhana at the same price.
  • Delhi Capitals paid INR 75 lakh for Kiran Navgire, the most expensive Indian sold, while 25 of the 27 available slots were filled across the five teams.
  • Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and England batter Sophia Dunkley went unsold, and Ireland's Orla Prendergast became the first Irish player sold at a WPL auction.

UP Warriorz signed Australia captain Sophie Molineux for INR 1.10 crore at the Women's Premier League auction for the 2027 season in Kochi on Wednesday, making the left-arm spin-bowling allrounder the most expensive buy of a mini auction in which 25 players were sold. Molineux's former franchise, defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru, pushed the bidding to INR 1.05 crore before dropping out, according to ESPNcricinfo. RCB had entered the auction with a purse of only INR 1.15 crore.

Molineux entered at a base price of INR 50 lakh. She was part of RCB's title-winning squad in 2024, missed the 2026 season, and led Australia to their seventh Women's T20 World Cup title in July. Cricinfo reported she is also Australia's highest wicket-taker this year.

Warriorz build around spin and power

UP Warriorz had the most work to do in Kochi. They arrived with eight slots to fill after releasing nine players, and INR 3.75 crore to spend, and they filled every slot. The franchise brought back Australian allrounder Grace Harris at her base price of INR 30 lakh, according to Cricbuzz. Harris made her WPL debut for UP Warriorz in 2023, spent three seasons there, and won the 2026 title with RCB after being released.

https://x.com/cricbuzz/status/2115418582364635547

The Warriorz also reunited with Asha Sobhana for INR 30 lakh. Sobhana had been bought for INR 1.10 crore at the previous auction before being released, Cricbuzz reported. India allrounder Sneh Rana and wicketkeeper-batter Sushma Verma joined at INR 30 lakh each, both at base price. Rana will play for her fourth WPL team, after RCB, Gujarat Giants and Delhi Capitals in the first four seasons.

"[We were going to get Molineux] at any cost. That puts us in a good position with Sophie and Grace combined to tweak our combinations and decide what works best."

— Kshemal Waingankar, UP Warriorz director of cricket

Waingankar said the plan is to pair Molineux's spin with Sophie Ecclestone's. Rana pointed to the spin group she joins alongside Deepti Sharma and said she was looking forward to playing under captain Meg Lanning.

Scotland captain Kathryn Bryce completed the Warriorz list at INR 10 lakh, with Manali Dakshini and Sahana Pawar. As an Associate player, Bryce can be fielded as a fifth overseas player.

Navgire leads the Indian buys

Delhi Capitals made the second-largest buy of the day, signing India batter Kiran Navgire for INR 75 lakh after Mumbai Indians pulled out at INR 70 lakh. Navgire was the most expensive Indian player sold. Delhi also bought 15-year-old Karnataka allrounder Uma Kashvi for INR 10 lakh, making her the youngest player sold at a WPL auction, and added Scotland's Kirstie Gordon and Nazma Khan at INR 10 lakh each.

Gujarat Giants signed wicketkeeper-batter G Kamalini for her base price of INR 40 lakh, after she played for Mumbai Indians in 2025 and 2026. Gujarat also bought Ireland allrounder Orla Prendergast for INR 30 lakh — the first Irish player sold at a WPL auction — and 16-year-old Samaira Raghav for INR 10 lakh.

Mumbai Indians, working with the smallest purse of INR 90 lakh, bought six uncapped Indian players, including Shweta Sehrawat for INR 20 lakh. Twelve of the 25 players sold were uncapped Indians. RCB, who bought no one in the first ten sets, added Australia allrounder Jess Jonassen for INR 40 lakh and South Africa allrounder Chloe Tryon for INR 30 lakh in the accelerated rounds, plus Tejal Hasabnis and Vrinda Dinesh.

Big names left unsold

Two established internationals found no buyer. Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu, at a base price of INR 30 lakh, and England batter Sophia Dunkley, at INR 50 lakh, both went unsold in a room where only 27 slots were available at the start and teams were protecting settled cores.

The fifth WPL edition starts on January 14, Cricbuzz reported, with Mumbai's CCI and Vadodara's Kotambi Stadium likely to host. The money went to spin-bowling allrounders and Indian power-hitting, with Molineux and Navgire setting the top prices in each market.
